summary: Milman Parry was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet before holding a post at Harvard University from circa 1929 to 1935.

Milo Cleveland Beach is an Indology and history/archaeology specialist who studied at Harvard. He held posts at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, Williams College, Fogg Art Museum, and served as Director of the National Museum of Asian Art.

Miloslav Krása was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Vincenc Pořízka at Charles University and at the University of Allahabad, later teaching at Charles University from 1954 to 1997.

Miloš Borecký worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Jan Rypka, as well as at the Sorbonne and Oxford, before holding posts at the National Library of the Czech Republic and the Library of Congress.

Milton Singer was a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and other fields. He completed his Ph.D. under Rudolf Carnap at the University of Chicago, where he later taught as Social Science Instructor and Professor of Anthropology from 1954 to 1979.

Min Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a postgraduate student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006) and holds an attested post as Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin pursued his studies under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Min Thu Wun was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied under Pe Maung Tin at the University of Rangoon from circa 1927 to 1935 and later studied at the University of Oxford from circa 1936 to 1939.
Minakshi Banerjee is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar and held a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society.
Ming Chen is a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Peking University.

Ming Mei specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned an MPhil from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and earned his Ph.D. under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en at UCLA, later serving as Professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Mingqian Xu specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and National Chengchi University, and worked as a Project Research Assistant at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts from 2013 to 2015.
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi.

Mini Verma is a scholar in Indology and other fields. She held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, Sai Group of Institutions, Institute of Management Studies, Noida, and Jagannath Institute of Management Sciences, Noida.

Minori Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata, Seiren Matsunami, and Kenyu Mitomo, holding posts at Taisho University, Sanko Cultural Institute, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Minoru Hara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Minoru Inaba works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kyoto University, he worked at Tokuyama Corporation, as Assistant Professor at Kyoto University, and as Professor at Doshisha University.

Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa, and served as Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1966 to 1993.

Minton Warren was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University, the American School of Classical Studies in Rome, and Harvard University.
